# Decisions — 001-audiobook-recap

Every product decision taken on this feature with nobody at the wheel, in the shape `commands/cruise.md`
shows and `make check-decisions` holds. A person confirms an entry by setting its **Status** to
`confirmed by human <date>`, or overturns it with an entry of their own; whoever records that answer writes
the `decision` line carrying the entry's id to the deck log, which closes the question the board shows.

## D1 — Which bounded contexts does 001-audiobook-recap touch?
- **Stage:** model · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:12:57Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** Which bounded contexts does the audiobook recap feature touch — which groups of the model's slices change on their own, each under one holder — and does every stream of `docs/event-model/model.yaml` sit in exactly one of them?
- **Options:** (a) one context, `recap` — every slice serial behind one captain; (b) two — `preparation` and everything the listener does, `listening`; (c) **three — `library`, `preparation`, `catch-up` — recommended.** The evidence, read off the model and the specification. First the streams, interrogated before any was named (nine-steps.md, *Interrogate every stream*); each `because` is also the `streams` block of `model.yaml`:

  | Stream | Slices that write it | The decision that needs one expected-version check, by requirement | Groups it spans, and why they stay together |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `preparation-{audioHash}` | PR1–PR4 | one transcription per content hash: a second import of identical audio must see preparation already started (FR-023 spec.md:269, US2 #6 spec.md:67) | transcription, indexing, discard: the audio is discarded only once every chapter is transcribed, a closure the transcription group sets and the discard group checks (FR-020 spec.md:266, FR-024 spec.md:270) |
  | `book-{bookId}` | LB3, LB4, LB5, LB11 | an EPUB is aligned against the chapters this import detected, by title and ordinal, in one decision over both (FR-021 spec.md:267, FR-022 spec.md:268) | import and ebook: the alignment decision reads both; a server book's audio is fetched once (LB5) |
  | `listening-{bookId}` | LB6–LB10 | the later-timed position wins: a report from the player, an entry by hand or the server's progress is adopted only if later than the position held (FR-028 spec.md:277, edge case spec.md:221) | player reports, manual entry, server sync, push: every one decides against the same held position; the gap an offer names is the last-listened time held here (FR-011 spec.md:248, US6 #2 spec.md:138) |
  | `connection-{listenerId}` | LB1 | one connection at a time; a renewed token replaces a rejected one and nothing is pushed through a lapsed connection (FR-029 spec.md:278, US6 #5 spec.md:141) | one group |
  | `settings-{listenerId}` | LB2 | last write wins on a form the listener edits; nothing decides against it (FR-035 spec.md:290, A3 spec.md:343) | one group — a `crud: true` event with its reason |
  | `catch-up-{bookId}` | CU1–CU5, CU7, CU8 | a recap at one tier and position is generated at most once, so two requests at one key must not both generate (FR-008 spec.md:242, US1 #7 spec.md:47) | offer, recap, voice: an offer is answered by a request or a decline at most once (FR-011, SC-003 spec.md:326); a recap is heard and rated against one that was generated (FR-007 spec.md:241, FR-037 spec.md:298); the voice chosen applies to every later recap and answer (FR-034 spec.md:289) |
  | `question-{questionId}` | CU10, CU11 | a question is answered or refused exactly once, against the position it was asked at (FR-014 spec.md:254, FR-015 spec.md:255) | one group; nothing spans a question and a recap, so they are separate streams correlated by `bookId` |
  | `spoiler-report-{reportId}` | CU15 | a report is recorded once and nothing decides against it afterwards (FR-038 spec.md:299, SC-002 spec.md:325) | one event, correlated by id to the recap, answer or entry it names |

  Then the candidates `make seams` groups from those streams, and the three tests over every seam between them (bounded-contexts.md, *The Seam Tests*). Line numbers are `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` unless a file is named:

  | Candidate | Streams it writes (slices) · views | Language | Change | Flow | What crosses | Confidence |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `library` | `book`, `listening`, `connection`, `settings` (LB1–LB11) · LB12–LB14 | *book* is a library entry with title, author, chapters from the file metadata and a server item (Key Entities :310, FR-022 :268); *chapter* is a navigation unit (FR-032 :284); *position* is to the second with the time it was last updated, from player, server or manual entry (FR-028 :277, :311) | the Audiobookshelf API version pin (edge case :223), import sources (FR-033 :285), the two-devices rule (:221) and the player (FR-032 :284) change here and reach neither the gradient nor transcription | the Listener and their server decide; hands off `BookImported`, `AudioFetched`, `ListeningResumed` and the position events, which the other two only fold | out: 8 events folded by preparation and catch-up (`make seams`); in: nothing — no other context writes a library stream, and LB12–LB14 fold the others' events as views | high that these four streams are one context: one actor, one job, and one change (FR-029 :278, US6 :129–141) that reaches connection, server book and position together |
  | `preparation` | `preparation` (PR1–PR4) | *book* is a content hash with chapters, never a title or author (FR-023 :269, FR-003 :237); *chapter* is a transcription unit, "one or more segments" where metadata is missing (FR-020 :266, edge case :218); no *window*, no *tier* | lazy transcription (FR-027 :273), audio retention (FR-024 :270), name canonicalisation (FR-026 :272), cost per book (SC-007 :330) and the legality of sharing by hash (A10 :350) change here alone; one-way cascade named: FR-010's digest (:244) and FR-018's per-chapter entries (:261) are extracted here for catch-up's display rule | Preparation acts on its own schedule once a book is added (Actors :27); hands off `ChapterTranscribed`, `ChapterIndexed`, `PreparationCompleted`; folds positions and settings only to bound the lazy policy | in: `BookImported`, `AudioFetched`, four position events, `SettingsChanged`; out: three events folded by catch-up and the library views. No command on either side reads the other's current state at decision time: coverage only grows, so a stale read refuses when it could have answered, never the reverse (FR-025 :271) | high — the clearest seam in the model: a different actor, a shared identity (the hash) the library does not have, and three tests passed |
  | `catch-up` | `catch-up`, `question`, `spoiler-report` (CU1–CU5, CU7, CU8, CU10, CU11, CU15) · CU6, CU9, CU12–CU14 | *window* exists only here (:313, FR-002 :236); *position* is the spoiler boundary at minute level including the partial chapter (FR-031 :280) and the cache key (FR-008 :242); *chapter* is a recency band, "the current chapter and the one before" (FR-005 :239); *book* is what a drafter must not be told the title of (FR-003 :237) | the gradient shares (FR-005 :239), tier lengths (FR-006 :240), the two-pass check (FR-004 :238) and the threshold default (FR-011 :248) change here and reach neither the player nor transcription; cascade named: a new tier adds an option to the settings form (FR-035 :290) | the engine decides the rules (constitution Principle I); the Listener triggers; the handoff in is `ListeningResumed`, folded only (CU2); after `RecapHeard` the player resumes on the client with no write back (FR-007 :241). Counter-signal: FR-013 (:250) puts the offer inside the listener's one gesture, two taps from play | in: `ListeningResumed`, `SettingsChanged`, four book events, three preparation events; `RequestRecap` carries its position as the listener's input (CU4), so no decision reads `listening` live; out: nothing written, nothing folded back | medium — the seam I am least sure of, below |

  The seams, one row each, and the two internal ones that keep each crowded context whole:

  | Seam | Verdict | The evidence that decided it |
  |---|---|---|
  | `library` ↔ `preparation` | two contexts | language: hash-book vs titled book, segment vs metadata chapter; change: FR-027/FR-024/A10 vs FR-029/FR-033; flow: Preparation (:27) vs Listener, event handoffs both ways |
  | `preparation` ↔ `catch-up` | two contexts | language: window and band vs transcript and segment; change: gradient and check vs transcription and retention; flow: both system actors, handoff `ChapterTranscribed`/`ChapterIndexed` folded only. One-way cascade (FR-010, FR-018) is a contract change to `ChapterIndexed`, not a shared decision |
  | `library` ↔ `catch-up` | two contexts, **least sure** | language: position to the second (FR-028) vs the minute-level boundary and cache key (FR-031, FR-008); change: tiers and gradient vs sync and player — neither reaches the other; flow: one event in (`ListeningResumed`), nothing back. Against: FR-013's two taps read as one actor's job, the settings form (FR-035) holds three of catch-up's values, and the Listener acts on both sides. For: US1 (:35–37) demonstrates the engine with no app, no player and no server — a context that ships without the other's streams |
  | within `library`: `book` · `listening` · `connection` · `settings` | one context | FR-029 (:278, US6 :129–141) is one change that reaches connection (LB1), server book (LB4, LB5) and position (LB9, LB10) at once — it cascades, so they are one; one actor, one job. `settings` stays as the listener's account-level form; three of its four values are catch-up's rules (FR-035 :290, research.md Q11 :185) — the first thing to move if the form grows |
  | within `catch-up`: `catch-up` · `question` · `spoiler-report` | one context | one window and one two-pass check govern recap, answer and who's who (FR-016 :256, FR-002–FR-004 :236–238); one refusal rule covers all three (FR-009 :243); one report names any of the three (FR-038 :299). A change to the window or the check reaches every group at once — the strongest merge signal in the model |

- **Decision:** three bounded contexts on `recap-api`, the directory rung of one deployable: `library` (LB1–LB14), `preparation` (PR1–PR4), `catch-up` (CU1–CU15). Every stream sits in one of them; `make seams` reports no stream written from two.
- **Why:** The listener's own things — their books, where they are, their server, their settings — change for platform reasons; turning audio into text changes for cost and provider reasons under an actor of its own and an identity (the content hash) the listener's book does not have; and the engine that refuses, drafts, checks and speaks changes for the one reason the product exists, the spoiler boundary. Each hands the next an event it only folds, and no command reads another's current state at decision time. · **Read against:** the specification (Actors :25–27, Key Entities :307–318, US1 :35–37, the requirements cited above), the constitution's Principle I, and this project's own convention — `docs/architecture.md` *Bounded contexts* puts several contexts in one service as `src/<context>/` behind a `public` module each, which is what `make check-imports` will hold; no standing entry, this is the first.
- **Why not split:** `library` holds 14 slices and `catch-up` 15, each serial behind one captain. No single stream invariant spans the streams inside either — that is why they are separate streams, correlated by id — so the reason each stays one context is the change test cascading, not a transaction: in `library`, FR-029 (:278) is one change reaching connection, server book and position together; in `catch-up`, FR-016 (:256) with FR-002–FR-004 (:236–238) makes one window and one check the rule for recap, answer and who's who, FR-009 (:243) one refusal, and FR-038 (:299) one report over all three. Splitting either along a stream would put one change on both sides of a seam.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the owner reads press play → offer → recap → resume (FR-013) as one job whose rules must change together, which merges `catch-up` into `library`; or A10's per-listener sharing opt-out makes preparation decide against listener state at transcription time, which merges `preparation` into `library`; or a decision turns out to need the position and the recap cache held still together, which puts `listening` and `catch-up` on one stream and so in one context.
- **Written to:** `docs/event-model/model.yaml`, `project.json`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/event-model/actors.yaml`
- **Status:** overridden by D31

## D2 — Is the automatic offer made when preparation has not yet reached the listener's position?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:22:08Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** US3 offers a recap on the first play after a gap (FR-011) and US2 #2 refuses a recap whose position preparation has not reached (FR-009, FR-025). The specification does not say whether the offer is made when both hold: a listener returning after nine days to a book prepared to chapter 8 while they are in chapter 9.
- **Options:** (a) make the offer and let the chosen tier end in the refusal; (b) **make no offer while coverage falls short — playback resumes, the player shows how far preparation has got, and the always-available button (FR-012) leads to the refusal — recommended**; (c) offer a recap up to the furthest covered position instead.
- **Decision:** (b). The offer is made only when preparation covers the position.
- **Why:** The offer is a promise of a recap in two taps (FR-013, SC-012), and a promise that ends in a refusal is what teaches a listener to decline the next one, which is the metric the offer exists for (SC-003). A recap to a position short of the listener's would be a recap of somewhere they are not, and the ending sentence (FR-007) could not name where they left off. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-009 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`, FR-011, FR-012, FR-013, FR-025, US2 #2, US3), the constitution's Principle I, and the model, whose `CU2` offer already runs inside the play request; no standing entry covered it and this project has no convention yet.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** beta listeners say they wanted to be told at the offer that preparation was still catching up, rather than finding it on the player — then (a) with a different message, never (c).
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-011, US3 #8, Edge Cases), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (CU2 reads coverage)
- **Status:** standing

## D3 — Does changing a book's voice regenerate its cached recaps?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:22:08Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-008 caches a recap per book, tier and position and regenerates only on movement; FR-034 says a book's voice choice applies to its recaps and answers. The specification does not say what a voice change does to a recap already generated and cached at the current position.
- **Options:** (a) **the drafted and checked text stays cached; the voice is presentation, so a changed voice re-speaks the cached text the next time it is played, with no redraft and no second spoiler check — recommended**; (b) the voice is part of the cache key and a change regenerates the whole recap; (c) a voice change applies only to recaps generated afterwards.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** The words a listener rated (FR-037) and may have reported (FR-038) should not change under them because they picked a different narrator; and a redraft is a second drafting pass that costs money (SC-007) and is a second chance for a spoiler for no gain, since the two-pass check (FR-004) guards text, not voice. (c) would leave a listener who just chose a voice hearing the old one at the position they are at. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-003, FR-004, FR-008, FR-034, FR-037 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), the constitution's Principle I, and the model (`CU5` speaks the recap in the book's voice; `CU1` records the choice); no standing entry covered it.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the speech provider's cost per re-speak turns out to exceed the drafting cost, which would make (c) the cheaper reading.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-008, FR-034), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (CU6 reads VoiceChosen)
- **Status:** standing

## D4 — How often is the offer made while a gap stands?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:22:08Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-011 offers a recap "on resume after a gap". The specification does not say whether a listener who declines and presses play again a minute later is offered again, or what restarts the gap.
- **Options:** (a) **once per return: the first play after a gap at or over the threshold carries the offer, accepting or declining answers it, and the next offer needs a new gap measured from the last-listened time, which playback restarts — recommended**; (b) offer on every play while the last-listened time is still over the threshold; (c) suppress offers for the rest of the day after a decline.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** A declined offer repeated on the next tap is nagging, and SC-003 counts acceptance of offers, so every repeat is a refusal in the numerator for free. Restarting the gap from the last-listened time is what FR-028 already records, and it means a listener who declines, listens for an hour and comes back next week is offered again, which is the product. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-011, FR-028, US3 #2–#3 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), and the model, whose `CU2` read model already keys offers by resumption ("not yet offered for") and whose `CU3` refuses a second answer to one offer; no standing entry covered it.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** beta listeners who declined by accident ask for the offer back and the always-available button (FR-012) is not found — then (b) once more after a decline, never more.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-011, US3 #9)
- **Status:** standing

## D5 — What is spoken when the spoiler check strips most or all of a draft?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:22:08Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-004 strips every sentence of a draft that references a person, place or event absent from the window, and FR-006 gives each tier a target length. The specification does not say what happens when the check leaves the draft far short of its tier, or empty.
- **Options:** (a) **speak what survives, without padding or redrafting; when nothing survives, refuse the request (FR-009) with that reason — recommended**; (b) redraft once with the stripped references forbidden, then speak what survives; (c) refuse whenever the survivor is under half the tier's length.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** The second pass is the guarantee (Principle I); a redraft is a second draft that needs a second check, costs a second pass (SC-007) and reopens the thing the first check closed. A short recap is a complete one — nothing in it is past the position — and a refusal with its reason (FR-009) is what the listener already gets when there is nothing to work from. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-004, FR-006, FR-009 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), the constitution's Principle I, and the model (`CU5` already records sentences stripped on `RecapGenerated` and reasons on `RecapRefused`); no standing entry covered it.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the phase 1 outside readers (SC-009) find stripped recaps incoherent often enough that one bounded redraft is worth its cost — a product decision for a person, since it widens the drafting surface.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-004, Edge Cases), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (CU5 RecapRefused reason)
- **Status:** standing

## D6 — Does aligning an EPUB after recaps were cached invalidate them?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:22:08Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-021 prefers aligned ebook text over the transcript for recap content and FR-008 regenerates a cached recap only when the position has moved. The specification does not say whether a recap cached from the transcript is played again after an EPUB is aligned at the same position.
- **Options:** (a) the cached recap stands until the position moves; (b) **the cache key includes the content the window was drawn from, so aligning an EPUB changes the key and the next request at the same position regenerates from the text — recommended**; (c) aligning an EPUB clears every cached recap and answer for the book at once.
- **Decision:** (b).
- **Why:** The listener attached the EPUB "for better accuracy", and the next recap they ask for is the one they will judge it by; keying the cache by content keeps FR-008's reason — one generation per key, nothing generated twice — while letting the key say honestly what the recap was built from. (c) spends generations nobody asked for. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-008, FR-021, US2 #4 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), and the model (`CU5` already reads `EbookAligned` and its window names the text where aligned); no standing entry covered it.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the owner would rather a transcript-built recap stand so a listener never hears two different recaps of one position — then (a), with the key unchanged.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-008, Edge Cases), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (CU5 cache key)
- **Status:** standing

## D7 — In companion mode, what gesture is the return that carries the offer?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:32:41Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-011 makes the offer on the first play after a gap, but an Audiobookshelf listener presses play in Audiobookshelf (US6 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`); the phase 2 gate (SC-010) measures offer acceptance among exactly those listeners, and the model's CU2 folded only `ListeningResumed`, which companion mode never raised.
- **Options:** (a) **opening the connected book in Recap after a gap at or over the threshold is the return and carries the offer, the gap measured from the server's last-listened time — recommended by the survey**; (b) no automatic offer in companion mode, the button only, with SC-010 restated.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** Opening the book in Recap is the only gesture Recap sees from a companion listener, and without it the beta's one metric cannot be measured; US6 #2 already measures the gap from the server's last-listened time. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-011, US6 #2, SC-010 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`); the model (`LB6` raises the return, `CU2` folds it); D4 (once per return); no convention yet
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the Audiobookshelf community says the offer should arrive inside their player, which is a platform integration this project does not own
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-011, US6 #6), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (LB6 return gesture)
- **Status:** standing

## D8 — Is a generated recap shared across listeners at the same content hash?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:32:41Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-023 said cached recaps were kept by content hash; FR-008 caches per book; the constitution's Principle IX forbids sharing transcript-derived text across accounts, and a recap is such text. The cache key also decides whether the recap lives on `catch-up-{bookId}` (D1) or on the hash.
- **Options:** (a) **private per book: recaps, answers, ratings and reports are the listener's book's, cached server-side for that book and never served to another account; only the transcription and the who's-who index are shared by hash — recommended by the survey**; (b) shared by hash, with Principle IX narrowed to the raw transcript, which a person would have to amend.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** It keeps Principle IX exact as written, matches the stream D1 chose, and costs only a second listener's first recap at a shared position; (b) is not available to this run, because it would loosen a constitution MUST. · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle IX), the specification (FR-008, FR-023 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), D1 (`catch-up-{bookId}`), the method's rule that no decision waives a MUST
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** a person amends Principle IX to allow derived text to be shared by hash, after the legal advice A10 waits on
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-023)
- **Status:** awaiting human confirmation

## D9 — What does the listener see when generation fails for a reason other than refusal?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:32:41Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-009 was the only failure outcome the specification knew; a drafting, checking or speech provider can time out, error or rate-limit while the listener sits with playback paused (US3 #2 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), and the constitution's Principle VI wants every provider failure mapped to a domain outcome.
- **Options:** (a) **"Couldn't catch you up right now" with Retry and Skip; Skip resumes playback; the offer stays answered; nothing partial is spoken or cached; the failure is recorded with its cause — recommended by the survey**; (b) silent fallback to playback with the button as the retry; (c) automatic retries before (a).
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** The listener accepted an offer and must be told why nothing is playing and how to get on; keeping the offer answered keeps D4 and SC-003 honest; recording the cause is what makes the failure count (Principle VI). (c) is a plan-level choice inside (a), not a different outcome. · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle VI), the specification (FR-009, FR-013, US3 #2 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), D4, D5 (a refusal is not a failure); no convention yet
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** beta listeners treat Retry as the common path, which argues for (c)'s bounded automatic retry inside the same screen
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-042, Edge Cases), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (CU5 RecapFailed, CU11 AnswerFailed, CU6 and CU12 read them)
- **Status:** standing

## D10 — What happens when a chapter cannot be transcribed after retries?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:32:41Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-020 transcribed resumably and FR-024 discarded audio only on completion (`specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`); a preparation that never completes had no end state the listener could see and kept their audio for ever, against Principle IX's retention obligation.
- **Options:** (a) **preparation is marked failed at that chapter with the reason; the library says "Couldn't prepare past Ch. N" and offers a retry; recaps and questions keep working up to coverage; the audio is discarded 7 days after the last failed attempt — recommended by the survey**; (b) retry indefinitely and keep the audio; (c) fail the whole book and discard everything including coverage already earned.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** It honours FR-025's partial coverage, bounds retention, and tells the listener a stuck book from a slow one; (c) throws away what the listener already paid for. · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle IX), the specification (FR-020, FR-024, FR-025, US2 #3 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), the model (`PR2`, `PR4`, `LB12`, `LB14`); no convention yet
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the transcription provider's own retry semantics make a 7-day window the wrong unit — the number is the plan's to tune, the shape is not
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md` (Clarifications, FR-020, FR-024, US2 #9, Edge Cases), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (PR2 ChapterTranscriptionFailed, PR4 discards after 7 days, LB12 and LB14 show it)
- **Status:** standing

## D11 — Can a listener remove a book, and what is deleted?
- **Stage:** specify · **Slice:** chart · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:32:41Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-036 let the library grow and nothing let it shrink (`specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`); positions, free-text questions and ratings are personal data in an append-only log, and Principle IX wants erasure designed before the first such event is persisted.
- **Options:** (a) **yes: everything keyed to the listener's book goes — position, last-listened time, recap cache, questions, answers, ratings, reports — and the hash-keyed transcription and index stay for other listeners; account closure erases the same way under Principle IX and has no screen in v1 — recommended by the survey**; (b) no removal in v1, closure only through A9's retention.
- **Decision:** (a).

## D20 — In what order do several imported files' chapters run?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** LB3 · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:43:09Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** A listener imports a book as several M4B/MP3/M4A files. Files may carry disc and track numbers in their tags; a listener may select them in any order; file names usually sort naturally. `BookImported.chapters` (numbered 1..N across the files) and `audioHash` (over the files' bytes in order) both depend on which order the files are taken in (Q1, `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB3/examples.md`).
- **Options:** (a) disc/track tags where every file carries them, otherwise the files' names in natural sort order; the listener's selection order is ignored; (b) the order the listener selected them in; (c) something else the artifacts support better. The stage made no recommendation.
- **Decision:** (a), made total so a test can pin it. The order of a book's files is a function of the files alone, never of the request: (1) where every file carries a track number, by disc then track, a file without a disc number counting as disc 1, provided no two files share a (disc, track) pair; otherwise (2) by file name without its directory, in natural sort order — runs of digits compared as numbers, the rest case-insensitively, so `part-2` comes before `part-10`; a tie on name (3) by the file's own content digest. The listener's selection order is not an input and the event does not record it. `audioHash` is computed over the files' bytes concatenated in that order, and `chapters` are numbered 1..N across the files in that order. No reorder step is added to this slice: a book whose order came out wrong is visible in its chapter list (LB12) and is re-imported after renaming in v1; a reorder affordance is a later slice's, if the beta asks for it.
- **Why:** Two listeners who own the same three files must get the same hash, or one transcription becomes two and the second listener waits ten minutes instead of one (US2 #6, SC-006, FR-023). The hash is "computed from the bytes the service received, never taken from the request" (R3) — and which finger tapped which file first is the request. The chapter order has to follow the same rule as the hash, because the shared preparation is one transcript in chapter order (FR-020, `preparation-{audioHash}` in D1): if `ada` and `ben` shared a hash but numbered their chapters differently, chapter 13's transcript would be a different chapter for each of them, and the spoiler boundary would be held against the wrong text. Tags first because they are the publisher's statement of the order and are inside the bytes the hash already covers; names second because a multi-part audiobook's names sort naturally in practice and a rule that falls back to nothing is not a rule; the digest tie-break only so the order is total. Ignoring selection order costs the listener nothing they can see on the mock-up, which has no reorder control. · **Read against:** the specification (US2 #1 and #6, FR-020, FR-022, FR-023, SC-006 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`); the constitution (Principle I — the boundary is held per chapter and position, so chapter numbering must be one thing per hash; Principle III — stream identity, here `preparation-{audioHash}`, is written down; Additional Constraints — event data records facts true on any machine, which a selection order is not); D1 (the preparation stream is keyed by the hash and `BookImported` is folded by nine slices); D8 (what is shared by hash); the LB3 examples R2 and R3. `.specify/product-owner.md` is a placeholder on every section, so no owner priority or taste was available and the decision rests on the specification and the constitution. Cites: none — `.specify/domain/` holds only its README; "natural sort" is defined in the decision itself rather than cited.
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-fable-5-1)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** A10's legal advice turns sharing by hash off for good — then the hash no longer needs to agree across listeners and (b), with a reorder step on the import screen, becomes available; a beta where tagged books come out misordered would add a reorder slice, not reverse this rule.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB3/examples.md` (R2's heading and bullets restated to this rule; Q1 closed; LB3-13 to LB3-15 added), `docs/adr/0002-file-order-and-content-hash-derive-from-the-files.md` (Proposed), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (LB3 block: the command's data line says the order; the chapters and the hash keep their shape and no field is added).
- **Status:** standing

## D21 — What is a book called when its files carry no title tag or disagree, and a chapter when its mark has no title?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** LB3 · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:43:29Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The model's `ImportBook` takes "title and author from the file tags" and says nothing of their absence or disagreement (Q2, `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB3/examples.md`). `BookImported`, which nine slices steer by, carries `title`, `author` and `chapters[].title`; the library card (LB12) and the player (LB13) read them, and the drafting step must never be told the first two (FR-003). What is the book called when no file carries a title tag, or the files disagree on title or author — and what is a chapter called when its chapter mark has no title?
- **Options:** (a) the first file's title and author tags; where there is no title tag, the first file's name without its extension; where there is no author tag, no author (an empty value the screens render as nothing, never a made-up name); a chapter mark with no title is "Chapter N"; (b) refuse the import until the listener types a title (a screen state this slice would then need); (c) something else the artifacts support better. The stage recommended none.
- **Decision:** (a), with its shape tightened so that nothing absent is stored as an invented value. **Title:** the title tag of the first file — in the order R2 gives the files, the file chapter 1 comes from first — that carries a non-empty title tag; files that disagree are settled by that precedence. Where no file carries one, the first file's name without its extension, exactly as it is. A title is therefore always present and never empty. **Author:** the author tag of the first file, in the same order, that carries a non-empty one; where none does, the book has no author — `author` is optional on `ImportBook` and `BookImported`, absent rather than an empty string or "Unknown", and a screen prints nothing for it (the card's "R. Okafor · 31 chapters · 14h 20m" becomes "31 chapters · 14h 20m"). **Chapter:** a chapter mark with no title gives a chapter with no title — `chapters[].title` is optional; every screen already names a chapter by its number first ("Chapter 14 · The Harbourmaster", `mockups/player.html`), so such a chapter shows as "Chapter 14" with nothing after the separator, which is the outcome (a)'s "Chapter N" wanted without writing a display default into the event. R2's segments keep their file-name titles: a file has a name; a bare mark has none. An empty or whitespace-only tag counts as absent, at the boundary where tags are parsed. The import never waits on the listener for a name; (b) is rejected.
- **Why:** The listener imported the files to be caught up, not to catalogue them. US2 #1 puts the book in the library the moment the files are in, with preparation already starting, and the approved mock-up goes from "Import audio files" straight to "Preparing" with no naming state between. The title is a label on the card and the player and nothing more: by FR-003 it is never handed to the drafting step, so a bare or file-named title cannot reach the one thing that would hurt the listener, while a refused import costs them the book and delays `BookImported`, which PR1 starts on (SC-006's ten minutes run from import). The files most likely to be untagged or tagged inconsistently are public-domain ones — the five books of the phase 1 gate (SC-009) — so (b) would block exactly the segment the first gate is judged on. A made-up author or a "Chapter 14" written into the title field would be a presentation default stored as a permanent fact, and every screen would then need a second rule to tell it from a real one — the rule in two places Principle XV forbids; absence is the one representation no screen has to second-guess. The first-tagged-file precedence is one rule that answers both absence and disagreement, and "first" is already defined by R2's file order, so it tracks D20. The owner brief is a placeholder in every section, so this is decided from the specification, the constitution and the standing entries alone. · **Read against:** the specification (US2 #1 and its Independent Test, FR-003, FR-022, Key Entities *Book*, SC-006, SC-009, edge case *chapter metadata missing or wrong* `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`); the constitution (XV — illegal states unrepresentable, one meaning per term; VIII — additive schemas, so optionality is fixed now, before the first event; XIV — an event field is a stop-and-ask, and this entry is that ask answered as the owner); the approved mock-ups (`mockups/add-book.html` has no naming state; `mockups/library.html` is the author line; `mockups/player.html` prints number then title); the model (`LB3` block; D1 — preparation's book "is a content hash … never a title or author", so no decision downstream reads the title; D19 — LB3 heads the library, so this is the first event written and its schema is set here rather than migrated later); R2 of the example map (file order, a segment titled after its file). Cites: none — `.specify/domain/` holds only its README; decided from the artifacts above. (The ID3/MP4 tag and chapter-atom conventions the parsing will meet are domain facts a person could file there; none is written yet, so none is cited.)
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-fable-5-1)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the owner wants the listener to confirm or type the title before preparation starts — option (b), which adds a naming state to this slice's screen. Changing the precedence rule (first tagged file → majority, or a trailing-number strip on the file name) is a refactor inside this decision, not a reversal of it.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB3/examples.md` (R1 widened with the title, author and chapter-title rules; LB3-17 to LB3-20; Q2 closed), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (LB3 block: the command's and the event's data lines), `docs/adr/0003-book-imported-title-and-author.md` (Proposed)
- **Status:** standing

## D22 — The same listener imports the same audio again under a new `bookId`: a second book, or a refusal?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** LB3 · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:43:31Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** Q3 in `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB3/examples.md`. The listener who already holds *Nine Winters at Halvard* as `nw-1` imports byte-identical copies of the same three files under a new client-minted `bookId`, so the content hash is the same. The specification parked this as nice-to-have (Clarifications, *Parked*; `story-split.md` *Parking Lot*) and sent it to the first slice that meets it, which is this one. Does the import produce a second book, or is it refused naming the book already in the library?
- **Options:** (a) a second book in the listener's library — its own stream `book-{bookId}`, its own position, recap cache and who's who; one preparation shared by hash, which PR1 already does; the slice writes one stream and nothing else; (b) refused, naming the book already held — a decision across two streams ("does this listener already hold this hash"), which the events port supports through its tag-conditional append (`appendIf`, the Dynamic Consistency Boundary in `apps/recap-api/src/application/ports/events.ts`) but which puts that mechanism into the first slice of the walking skeleton; (c) something the artifacts support better. The stage recommended none.
- **Decision:** (a). A new `bookId` is a new book. The import is accepted, `BookImported` lands as the first event on the new stream carrying the same `audioHash`, preparation is not started again, and the earlier book is untouched. Nothing is added to the `ImportBook` command and no refusal is added to the LB3 block. Resolved in the example map as a bullet and a scenario under R3 (*the same bytes give the same hash whoever imports them* — "whoever" now includes the same listener), and Q3 closed.
- **Why:** The listener asked for a book and the specification says a library never refuses one: US9 #2, "there is no limit that refuses it", and US9 gives each book "its own position, recap cache and who's-who index, independent of the others" — which is exactly what two books with one hash get. The accidental case is already handled: R4 (LB3-7) makes the client-minted `bookId` the idempotency key, so a retried or double-sent import appends nothing and returns the original; a *new* `bookId` is therefore a deliberate second add, not a slip the service should second-guess. It costs the listener nothing: PR1's `StartOnReceipt` "starts once per hash; skipped when the hash is already being prepared", so the second book is recap-ready within SC-006's one minute, the same as US2 #6's second listener. Removal works without a special case: LB15 deletes what is keyed to one `bookId` and leaves the hash-keyed transcript (D11, FR-043), so removing one copy leaves the other, and re-importing a book after removing it — the natural way to start a book over — is simply a new book; under (b) the refusal would have to fold `BookRemoved` across streams to allow that. Principle II does not decide between the two — (b) would check the write model through the tag condition, which is allowed — but the constitution's simplicity rule does: "the smallest design satisfying the spec wins" and an added mechanism "MUST be justified in the plan against a named requirement", and no requirement asks for this refusal. Principle V's walking-skeleton rule points the same way: D19 put LB3 first so the skeleton is import → prepare → request → hear, and a cross-stream boundary in that slice is a new architectural shape no capability has earned; the port's own note says the stream is the boundary "until" a decision cannot be guarded by one stream's version, and this one can. What the listener sees (LB12): two rows titled *Nine Winters at Halvard*, each with its own progress and its own "recap ready"; `BookImported` already carries `importedAt` and `audioHash`, so LB12 can tell the rows apart or mark them as the same audio without a new field — that is LB12's to decide, not this slice's. · **Read against:** the specification (US9 #2, US9 lead, US2 #6, FR-023, FR-036, FR-043, SC-006 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`; Clarifications *Parked* line), the constitution (Principle II, Principle V *Slice independence* and *One capability per slice*, Additional Constraints *Simplicity governs*), standing D8 (recaps per book, so the two books cache separately), D11 (what removal deletes), D19 (LB3 heads the skeleton), the model (LB3 `book-{bookId}`; PR1 `StartOnReceipt`; LB15; LB12), the port's own guidance on when the DCB is read (`events.ts`), and the LB3 map's R3 and R4. `.specify/product-owner.md` is a placeholder in every section and gave no taste rule on library tidiness. Cites: none — `.specify/domain/` holds only its README; decided from the specification and the constitution.
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-fable-5-1)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the owner, when the brief is filled in, says a listener's library must hold each audio at most once — a taste rule nothing written states — in which case (b) is the decision, added as a refusal on `ImportBook` guarded by `appendIf` over a listener-and-hash tag, in a later slice rather than this one; books already imported twice stay as they are.

## D23 — How does the catch-up context know a book is the signed-in listener's?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** CU1 · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:50:15Z · **Stream:** catch-up
- **Question:** R5 (another listener's book, or no book, is *not found*) is required by the constitution's Principle IX, and the model gives `CU1` no `reads`: nothing in its block folds `BookImported` or `ServerBookAdded`, whose `listenerId` is the only place ownership is recorded. The same question stands for every later catch-up command slice (`CU4`, `CU10`, `CU15`).
- **Options:** (a) `CU1` — and every later catch-up command slice — gains a `reads:` of the library's `BookImported` and `ServerBookAdded`, which re-renders `specs/001-audiobook-recap/chart.yaml` so each steers by `LB3`'s and `LB4`'s marks and waits for those slices to plan; (b) **the catch-up context asks the library context through one application port of its own — *is this book the listener's* — answered in production by the library's `public` module once it exists, by a fake in tests, and in the meantime by a driven adapter that reads the opening event of `book-{bookId}` for its `listenerId` — recommended by the stage**; (c) the HTTP edge decides — ruled out by Principle IX.
- **Decision:** (b), taking the stage's recommendation, with three constraints the stage's wording left open. **The port is catch-up's**, named for the conversation and not the technology (Principle IV) — something like `ListenersLibrary.holds(listenerId, bookId)`, the plan's to name — and it answers **only yes or no**: catch-up never learns whether a book exists, so it cannot leak existence, and CU1-5 and CU1-6 refuse identically by construction. **Every implementation answers from the write model**: the opening event of `book-{bookId}` (`BookImported` or `ServerBookAdded`, both of which carry `listenerId`), read as a tolerant reader (Principle VIII) — never from a library projection such as `LB12`'s, because a command that needs to know whether something happened checks the write model and never a read model (Principle II). **The use case asks before it decides**: the Decider stays pure and folds `VoiceChosen` alone; the not-found is the use case's refusal, observable at the level Principle V binds acceptance to, and the examples stay *Given* synthetic `BookImported` on `book-{bookId}` as they are written, which is what the fake is seeded from. Every later catch-up command slice reuses this one port rather than growing a `reads`.
- **Why:** The listener's library is the library's to know and catch-up's to ask, not to copy. Ownership is a fact written once at import and never revised — a book is `ada`'s from `BookImported` on, and only `BookRemoved` (`LB15`, parked as Q6) ever touches it — so asking it is not a race against anything the append must hold still, and D1's sentence that *no command reads another's current state at decision time* holds: the voice decision is made against `catch-up-{bookId}` alone, and ownership is a precondition the use case checks through the one door D1 named, the library's `public` module (`docs/architecture.md`, *Bounded contexts*). Against (a) there are three things, any one of which would have decided it. First, the method refuses it: a `state-change` slice has "no `reads` — a command takes user input and folds events under the same guard it appends with, never a maintained view" (`docs/event-model/README.md`, *The four patterns*), and the chart is derived from `reads`, so (a) cannot be expressed without re-patterning four command slices into something they are not — a command fed by a maintained ownership view is exactly the `ReadModel → Command` dependency Principle III forbids. Second, it is a copy of a fact: a persisted ownership projection inside catch-up is a second place `listenerId` lives, lagging the first by design, and `BookRemoved` would then have to be folded there too or Q6 becomes a leak. Third, it stalls the fairway: with no `mark-set` line yet in either deck log, `LB4` unclaimed and sixth in the library's order, `CU1` and then `CU4`, `CU10` and `CU15` would each sit *blocked* on the library for a fact one in-process call answers. (c) puts an authorisation decision in a driving adapter, which Principle IX forbids outright and the stage rightly ruled out. · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle IX: "Authorisation MUST be enforced server-side on every request, inside the application rather than in a driving adapter alone. Cross-tenant access MUST return not-found, not forbidden"; Principle II, the write-model rule; Principle III, "A `ReadModel → Command` dependency MUST NOT exist"; Principle IV, ports named for the business conversation with a usable fake); the specification (Key Entities *Listener*: "owns a library, settings and, per book, a position, voice choice and last-listened time"; *Book*: "an audiobook in a listener's library"; A2; FR-034; FR-043's "remove a book from their library"); D1 (the three contexts, the `public` module as the seam, and the sentence quoted above — kept, not overridden); D8 and D11 (what is the listener's book's and what is shared by hash); this project's convention in `docs/architecture.md` *Bounded contexts* ("one `public` module ... that is the whole of what the other contexts may import", held by `make check-imports`); the model (`LB3` and `LB4` both put `listenerId` on the book stream's opening event; `CU1` is `state-change` with `folds: [VoiceChosen]`); `docs/event-model/README.md` *The four patterns* and *`reads` and `folds` are different questions*. Cites: none — `.specify/domain/` holds no fact on this; decided from the constitution, the specification and the standing entries above.
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-fable-5-1)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the library becomes a service of its own (`docs/architecture.md`, rung 3), so the port can no longer be answered in-process from the book stream — at which point ownership crosses the seam as events and catch-up maintains a persisted ownership view folding `BookImported`, `ServerBookAdded` and `BookRemoved`, which is (a) done honestly as an automation's todo list rather than as a command's `reads`.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/CU1/examples.md` (R5 rule line and scenarios CU1-5, CU1-6; Q1 closed; the port named under *Fixture* so R1–R4's BookImported givens say what they seed)
- **Status:** standing

## D26 — Does `VoiceChosen` carry `listenerId`?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** CU1 · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:52:00Z · **Stream:** catch-up
- **Question:** The model's `VoiceChosen` carries `bookId`, `voice`, `chosenAt`; the library's `BookImported` and catch-up's `SpoilerReported` carry `listenerId`. Principle IX wants personal data in the log erasable, and `CU5`, `CU6` and `CU11` steer by this event's fields, so the shape is a contract three slices build against.
- **Options:** (a) **keep the model's shape — the stream is the listener's book's, a voice name is not personal data, and who chose is already on every event's context as `actor_id` — recommended**; (b) add `listenerId` to the payload, which widens a mark three slices steer by for a field none of them reads.
- **Decision:** (a). `VoiceChosen { bookId, voice, chosenAt }` as modelled. The listener who chose is the append's `actor_id` in the event context the store already requires (`apps/recap-api/src/application/ports/event-context.ts`), and erasure follows the book: `LB15`'s removal erases "everything keyed to the listener's book" (D11), which `catch-up-{bookId}` is.
- **Why:** The three slices that speak in the voice need the book and the voice and nothing else; a field nobody reads is a field everybody has to carry for ever (Principle VIII). What a person could be identified by — who chose — is on the context, where every event of this service already records its actor, so nothing is lost by leaving the payload as the model drew it. · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle IX, erasure by reference or per-subject key; Principle VIII, a schema change is for ever); the model (`VoiceChosen` as drawn, `CU5`/`CU6`/`CU11` read `bookId` and `voice`); D11 (removal erases the listener's book's data); D8 (recaps and their kin are per book); the event-store port's `EventContext` (`actor_id` on every append) — this project's own convention; `.specify/domain/` holds no fact on this.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** erasure is implemented by crypto-shredding behind a per-subject key and the key has to be found from the payload rather than from the stream or the context — then the field is added as a mark change, with its ADR.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/CU1/examples.md` (Q5 closed; R1's fields unchanged)
- **Status:** standing

## D27 — Does a position entered by hand count as the last-listened time the gap is measured from?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB6 · **When:** 2026-10-21T13:50:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-011 measures the gap from the last-listened time, which FR-028 records per book. LB7's `ListeningStopped` carries it ("stoppedAt — the book's last-listened time") and LB9's `PositionSyncedFromServer` carries the server's; LB8's `PositionEntered` carries only `enteredAt`, and the specification does not say whether a position a listener typed in for a book played elsewhere (US7 #6) counts as having listened then. LB6 folds all four events to compute the days since last listened, so it has to know.
- **Options:** (a) **yes — the entry stands as the last-listened time and the gap runs from it — recommended**; (b) no — the gap runs from the last stop or server sync and ignores entries; (c) an entry clears the gap until the next stop.
- **Decision:** (a). The last-listened time is the latest instant the stream holds: a stop, the server's last-listened time, a hand-entered position's entry time, or an earlier resume.
- **Why:** A listener enters a position because they have just been listening elsewhere, up to there; the entry is the nearest thing Recap has to when they last listened, and (b) would offer a nine-day catch-up to somebody who typed in yesterday's position. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-011, FR-028, US7 #6 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), the model (`LB8`'s `PositionEntered` carries `enteredAt`; the `listening` stream's invariant names the last-listened time as held on that stream), D4 (playback restarts the gap) and D13 (whole 24-hour periods); no convention yet.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** beta listeners who enter positions for several books at once find the offer withheld on their first real play — then (c), with the entry clearing the gap until a stop.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB6/examples.md` (R2, scenario LB6-6)

## D28 — How does a command on the listening stream know the caller owns the book?
- **Stage:** plan · **Slice:** LB6 · **When:** 2026-10-21T15:55:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** Authorisation is a use-case decision about ownership (constitution IX; `AGENTS.md`, *Deployable ownership*), but the owner is recorded on the book's stream (`BookImported.listenerId`, LB3; `ServerBookAdded.listenerId`, LB4; ended by `BookRemoved`, LB15) and not on `listening-{bookId}`, which LB6 folds. Every command on the listening stream — LB6, LB7, LB8 — has to answer the same question, so it is a convention and not one slice's choice.
- **Options:** (a) **the use case reads `book-{bookId}` before the listening stream and folds it to an owner with a tolerant reader (type name and one field, no event type of its own); a caller who is not the owner, a book nobody imported and a removed book all answer `not-found` — recommended**; (b) carry `listenerId` on `ListeningResumed` and let the first writer own the stream; (c) a `guard` over tags spanning the book and listening streams; (d) trust the client's claim of ownership.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** The book's stream is the write model where ownership was recorded, and a command that needs a fact reads the write model (constitution II); the listening stream cannot establish ownership itself without making it a race any holder of a leaked `bookId` wins (b), and a guard (c) buys nothing because the owner never changes between read and append. Existence is not leaked: the three refusals answer alike. · **Read against:** the constitution (II, IX), `AGENTS.md` (*Deployable ownership*: what an account may do is a use-case decision about ownership; the HTTP adapter makes no authorisation decision), D22 (the stream stays the boundary for LB3), and this project's own convention — `oidc-keycloak.ts` says ownership is decided in the use case that loads the record, against the `Customer` it is handed; no standing entry covered it.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** a book becomes shareable between listeners — then ownership is a set and a `guard` over both streams replaces the read.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB6/research.md` (§1), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB6/data-model.md`, `docs/adr/0005-ownership-is-read-from-the-book-stream.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D30 — What is the write contract for a return: the route, its body and where the idempotency key rides?
- **Stage:** plan · **Slice:** LB6 · **When:** 2026-10-21T15:55:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The first write endpoint of the service sets the convention every later one copies (`skills/api-design`); the constitution (II) wants a caller-supplied idempotency key on every public write, and the model names `resumptionId` as the event's own identity (`identifies: resumption`).

- **Decision:** (a). The key is a body field rather than an `Idempotency-Key` header because it is part of the fact — the event's identity — and not transport metadata; the response body is `{ bookId, resumptionId, position, resumedAt, daysSinceLastListened?, via }`, exactly what the Player's status region reads.

- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** LB7 and LB8 want one position resource after all — then `resumptions` becomes one of three sub-resources of `position` and the body stays.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/contracts/LB6-resumptions.md`, `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB6/research.md` (§3)

## D33 — What happens to a position report whose instant is ahead of the service's own clock?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB7 · **When:** 2026-10-21T15:59:46Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The player reports a stop with `at`, which becomes the book's last-listened time on `listening-{bookId}`; the stream's rule is that the later-timed report wins and an earlier-timed one is refused `stale-report` (FR-028, the two-devices edge case; LB6 R4). A stop timed a day ahead by a device with a wrong clock would be held as the latest instant, and every correctly-timed report afterwards — a resume (LB6), a stop (LB7), a hand entry (LB8), the server's progress (LB9) — from any device would be refused as stale until real time passed it, and the gap LB6 computes (D13) would come out negative. LB6's gaps review parked this to LB7 as "accepted as given; `recordedAt` beside `occurredAt` is what makes it diagnosable later".
- **Options:** (a) accept the report as given — the domain has no clock (constitution IV) and cannot tell; the store's `recordedAt` beside `occurred_at` makes it diagnosable afterwards; (b) **the use case refuses a report timed later than the service's own now by more than a small tolerance (5 minutes) with its own error `clock-ahead`, so the stream never holds an instant from the future; `now` reaches the use case injected and the same rule holds for every writer of the stream — recommended by the stage**; (c) clamp a future-timed report to the service's now and record both instants.
- **Decision:** (b), as the stage recommended. A report whose `at` is more than 5 minutes after the service's now is refused `clock-ahead` — "this device's clock is ahead; the position was not saved" — with no events; the refusal names the service's instant so the screen can say by how much. A report within the tolerance is held as given, never clamped. `now` is a typed input beside `at`, supplied by the use case from a clock port with a fake (constitution IV); the domain reads no clock. The rule is the stream's, not this slice's: it holds for every writer of `listening-{bookId}` — LB6's resume, LB7's stop, LB8's entry and LB9's adoption of the server's `lastUpdate`, which is a third party's clock — so LB6, LB8 and LB9 inherit it as a standing rule rather than each deciding it. The 5 minutes is the conventional clock-skew tolerance (Kerberos's default); the number is the plan's to tune, the shape is not.
- **Why:** The later-timed-wins rule is a lock, and a future instant is a lock with no key: one wrong phone clock would freeze the listener's book — every stop refused, so the position no longer persists (US7 #3, FR-028); every resume refused, so no offer and no gap (FR-011); a hand entry refused too (LB8), so the one way to correct it by hand is also shut — until the calendar caught up, which for a clock a year out is never. "Diagnosable afterwards" (a) is an engineer reading a log, not a listener getting their position back; the listener cannot see `recordedAt` and the stream offers no command that overrides a held instant. (c) records a stop at a moment the listener did not stop at, which is a fact the system invented, and it does so silently, so a device that is wrong stays wrong and every report from it is quietly rewritten; the constitution keeps domain time and storage time apart precisely so a clock problem can be reconciled, and clamping is conflating them with extra steps. (b) refuses honestly, tells the listener the one thing they can fix, and leaves the stream exactly as it was, so a correctly-timed report from the next device is accepted. The tolerance keeps ordinary skew from refusing honest stops, and its cost is bounded: at worst the stream holds an instant five minutes ahead and refuses honest reports for five minutes as `stale-report`, which D13's whole-day floor never notices. A device whose clock is *behind* needs no new rule — its reports are already refused as earlier-timed (LB6 R4) and harm nothing. · **Read against:** the constitution (III: the Decider is pure and "Time and identifiers arrive as typed inputs"; IV: the domain imports no clock and every driven port has a fake; *Additional Constraints*: "Domain time (`occurredAt`, injected) MUST be stored separately from storage time (`recordedAt`). Conflating them makes clock problems unreconcilable", which rules (c) out and is what (a) leaned on for diagnosis rather than recovery), the specification (FR-028, FR-011, US7 #3, the two-devices edge case `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), standing D13 (whole 24-hour periods) and D27 (the last-listened time is the latest instant held, whatever wrote it), the model (`streams.listening.because` in `docs/event-model/model.yaml`: the later-timed position wins), and this project's own convention — LB6's examples R4 (`stale-report`, equal accepted) and research §5–§6 (`heldAt` folded from four events; `occurred_at` = the command's `at`, kept apart from the store's `recordedAt`, which `apps/recap-api/migrations/001_events.js` and `event-context.ts` already hold). `.specify/product-owner.md` is still the template, so it answered nothing here; this is decided from the specification, the constitution and the log. The 5-minute tolerance is an industry default, not a domain fact, and is marked as tunable for that reason.
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-fable-5-1)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the client ever has to report stops it observed offline hours earlier with a device clock the service cannot vouch for — then the report would carry the device's instant and the service's receipt separately and the rule would move to the receipt, which is (a) with the field that makes it safe.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB7/examples.md` (R6 and its examples), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/decisions.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D35 — What exactly does a hand-entered position record: whole minutes or seconds, which boundary, and whose instant?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB8 · **When:** 2026-10-21T16:13:12Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-030 says a position is entered "as chapter plus minutes" and the model's `EnterPosition` carries "chapter 12, 20 min", but the split's acceptance row quotes "Chapter 14, 32 minutes" → 4:03:17, which no whole number of minutes reaches (the mock-up's 32:10 does). The model says "refused when the minutes exceed the chapter" without saying whether exactly the chapter's length is beyond it. And the model's `enteredAt` could be stamped by the client, as every other writer of `listening-{bookId}` stamps its `at`, or by the service, which would make D27's last-listened time and D33's clock-ahead rule mean something different for this one writer.
- **Options:** (a) **whole minutes (FR-030); position = the chapter's start + minutes × 60, in seconds, from the book's own chapters on `book-{bookId}`; refused `beyond-chapter` only when the minutes exceed the chapter's length, equal accepted; refused `no-such-chapter` outside 1..N; the instant is the client's `at` at the moment of Confirm, the shape every writer of the stream sends — recommended**; (b) minutes and seconds, so the split's 4:03:17 is reachable; (c) the service stamps `enteredAt` with its own now, so an entry can never be stale or clock-ahead.
- **Decision:** (a). The split's 4:03:17 is read as the mock-up's position quoted loosely, not as a requirement for seconds: a listener who has been listening elsewhere knows the chapter and roughly the minutes, not the second (the research card: "chapter 12, about 20 minutes in"). The boundary is inclusive the way every boundary on this stream is — `stale-report`'s equal-accepted (LB6 R4), D33's "exactly five minutes is recorded" — so a chapter exactly 40:00 long accepts 40, which is the next chapter's first second. The client's `at` keeps one shape for the stream, so D27 (the entry is the last-listened time), D33 (clock-ahead) and the stale-report rule apply to an entry exactly as to a stop or a resume, with no fourth case for the fold. The event carries the position in seconds and not the chapter and minutes, because every reader of the stream folds a position and the chapter is derivable from the book's chapters.
- **Why:** The specification says minutes and the model says minutes; one looser row in the split does not outvote both, and it is the row that is wrong by ten seconds rather than the requirement. One instant-stamping rule for four writers is one fold rule for six readers. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-030, FR-028, US7 #6 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`), the model (`LB8`'s command and event; `streams.listening.because`), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/story-split.md` (the LB8 row and the parking lot's "manual minutes beyond the chapter (LB8 already refuses it)"), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/mockups/research.md` (*Manual position entry*), standing D27 and D33, and this project's own convention — LB6's `ResumeListening { position, at, resumptionId }` and LB7's `StopListening { position, at, stopId }` on the sibling branches; `.specify/product-owner.md` is still the template and answered nothing.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** a person says the form should take seconds too — then (b), with the same arithmetic and the same boundary at the chapter's last second.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB8/examples.md` (R1–R3, R5 and their scenarios), `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (the LB8 block's command and the event's attributes)
- **Status:** standing
