## D37 — Does moving the position backwards by hand warn the listener about the recap cache?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB8 · **When:** 2026-10-21T16:13:12Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The gap card asks "Moving backwards invalidates the cache and must reveal nothing between (edge case) — any warning?", and the research card lists a *confirm* state "that this replaces the tracked position and invalidates the recap cache (FR-008, A5)". A hand entry whose position is behind what is held is recorded when later-timed (the stream's rule, FR-028; LB7 R2 for a rewind), so the question is only whether the form says anything about the cache.
- **Options:** (a) **no warning beyond the preview and Confirm: the form reads the inputs back and the listener confirms; the cache is catch-up's rule, read off `PositionEntered` (A5, FR-008) — recommended**; (b) a warning when the new position is behind the held one ("this replaces your position; your recap will be regenerated"); (c) a two-step confirm for every entry.
- **Decision:** (a). Confirm is the confirmation the research card asks for; the preview is what makes it informed. The recap cache belongs to the catch-up context, which invalidates it when the position moves (FR-008, the *position moved backwards* edge case) without this form's help, and a warning here would be the library telling the listener about a rule it neither owns nor can see. Moving backwards is the common case for this form — the player reported further on than the listener really got — and warning on the common case teaches the listener to dismiss warnings.
- **Why:** A listener setting a position wants it set; the spoiler boundary (Principle I) is kept by catch-up regenerating at the new position, not by a dialog. · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle I; the context boundary D1/D31/D32 draws between where the position is written and where the recap is cached), the specification (FR-008, the *position moved backwards* edge case, A5), the model (`LB8` writes `listening-{bookId}`; `CU4`/`CU5` own the cache key), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/mockups/storyboard.html` and `research.md` (the two questions); no standing entry covered it.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the hand's walk or a beta listener sets a position by mistake and loses a recap they wanted kept — then (b), worded as what will happen rather than as a caution.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB8/examples.md` (R3, R8)
- **Status:** standing

## D38 — Does `ServerConnected` carry a count of the server's books?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB1 · **When:** 2026-10-21T16:23:55Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The LB1 block of `docs/event-model/model.yaml` draws the event as "listenerId, server books.home.lan, 2 new books in the library, connectedAt", and the AddBook mock-up (`docs/event-model/mockups/add-book.html`, the Audiobookshelf row) reads "Connected · books.home.lan · 2 new books in your library" — but that screen is LB4's, whose own frame says "the server's own list, fetched live". A count on the event is a permanent contract (Principle VIII), an event field is a decision an agent must ask about (Principle XIV), and three slices steer by this event's fields (LB5, LB10, LB12).
- **Options:** (a) `ServerConnected` carries `serverBooks`, the number of items the server listed at the moment of connection, and the views compute "new" by folding `ServerBookAdded` and subtracting; (b) **`ServerConnected` carries no count — `listenerId`, `connectionId`, `serverUrl`, `connectedAt` and nothing about the library; "2 new books in your library" is LB4's live read of the server's list minus the books already added, and the model frame's "2 new books in the library" becomes the AddBook card's line rather than an event field — recommended by the stage**; (c) the event carries the count of server books *not yet in the listener's library* — ruled out by the stage, since the command would have to read the library's read model at decision time.
- **Decision:** (b), the stage's recommendation. `ServerConnected { listenerId, connectionId, serverUrl, connectedAt }`, exactly as R1 and every LB1 scenario already name it. The frame data on the LB1 block loses "2 new books in the library"; the number stays where it is shown, on LB4's AddBook row, computed when that screen reads the server.
- **Why:** A listener connecting a server wants to know one thing — that Recap can reach it with that token — and the connection screen says so (R7: "Connected to books.home.lan"). How many books are on the server, and how many of them are *new*, is a fact about the server and the library on the day the listener looks, not about the moment they pasted a token: a count frozen on the event is wrong the first time they add a book in Audiobookshelf, and "new" cannot be derived from it at all, because the subtraction (a) proposes counts books added under the previous connection against a snapshot taken by the new one (R3: renewal is the ordinary case, and the books already added stay in the library per US6 #5). Nobody reads it: LB5 and LB10 fold the event to find the connection to reach the server *through*; LB12 shows "synced | unreachable | needs renewing"; LB4 fetches the list live. A field nobody reads is a field every reader carries for ever — the reasoning D26 applied to `VoiceChosen`, taken the same way here. (a)'s premise that "the connect fetched the list anyway" does not hold under R1 as written, which asks the server "the smallest question that proves the token — which account it belongs to"; a count would widen the adapter's call and its Principle VI failure enumeration for a number the slice never shows. (c) is not available: Principle III, *Commands read user input and the event stream only. A `ReadModel → Command` dependency MUST NOT exist.* · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle III, the ReadModel → Command rule and *every read-model field MUST trace to a source event*, which LB4's live-fetched row does not claim to; Principle VIII, event schemas are permanent and additive; Principle XIV, an event field is asked about; Additional Constraints, *Simplicity governs: the smallest design satisfying the spec wins*); the specification (US6 #1 "their library is listed and they can pick a book", US6 #5, FR-029, Key Entities *Audiobookshelf connection*: "a server URL and token belonging to a listener, with the last successful sync" — no count); the model (`streams.connection` `because`: one connection at a time, renewal replaces; LB4's frame "the server's own list, fetched live"; the `reads` of LB5, LB10, LB12); D1's seam table (`connection-{listenerId}` is one group, and the `library` row's view LB12 folds events as a view); D26 (a sibling event-field decision on `slice/CU1`: keep the modelled shape, carry nothing no reader needs); ADR 0004 (on `slice/LB3`: the event carries the listener's `sub` and nothing else about them). `Cites: none` — `.specify/domain/` holds only its README; whether Audiobookshelf's token-proving endpoint also returns library items is a fact about its published contract for the plan to cite, and the decision does not turn on it, because a count that arrived free would still be stale and unread. The owner brief is still its placeholder.
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-fable-5-1)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** a reader appears that must show the server's size *without* reaching the server — say the library list (LB12) is required to read "N books on your server" while the server is unreachable — in which case a total (never "new") is added as an additive field under Principle VIII, as a mark change with its ADR.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/examples.md` (Q1 closed; R1's bullets and the event's fields unchanged — they already name listenerId, connectionId, serverUrl, connectedAt), the LB1 block of `docs/event-model/model.yaml` (the ServerConnected frame's data drops "2 new books in the library"; its attributes are those four fields)
- **Status:** standing

## D39 — Is a plain `http://` Audiobookshelf server URL accepted when a listener connects, or must it be `https://`?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB1 · **When:** 2026-10-21T16:24:40Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** Q2 of `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/examples.md`. The call to the server is made by `recap-api`, which holds the listener's token and reaches the server through a driven port (A1, constitution VI), so the token travels from the service to the listener's own server over whichever scheme the URL names. Self-hosters on a home LAN commonly run Audiobookshelf without TLS at a name like `books.home.lan`; the model's own example is `https://books.home.lan`; FR-029 and US6 #1 say "URL and token" and name no scheme.
- **Options:** (a) `https://` only — refuse `http://` at the edge with a message saying why; (b) **both `http://` and `https://` accepted; the URL type admits the two schemes and nothing else; the screen says nothing special about http — recommended by the stage**; (c) both accepted, and the screen warns on `http://` that the token will travel unencrypted to that server.
- **Decision:** (b), as the stage recommended. The URL type admits exactly `http` and `https`; a URL with either is a connection request like any other, and R7's screen has no http-specific state. Which account the token belongs to, a certificate the adapter will not trust, and a server that does not answer all stay R2's three refusals — a TLS failure on an `https://` address is `server-unreachable`, not a scheme question, and whether the adapter trusts a self-signed certificate is the plan's, not decided here.
- **Why:** The server is the listener's own, on a path they chose to expose it by, and the token is that server's own credential — it is already there. Recap's obligation under Principle IX is over what *it* keeps: the token is held behind a port, in no event and no log (R5), whichever scheme carried it in. Refusing `http://` would turn away the first segment the PRD targets — SC-010's beta is "10 beta users from the Audiobookshelf community" — on the evidence of a letter in the address: a self-hoster who reaches their server over a VPN or a tunnel types `http://` and the wire is encrypted at a layer the URL does not name, so (a) refuses a safe case and (c) warns falsely about it, and a warning that is wrong for part of its audience is one the rest learn to ignore. Audiobookshelf's own app, Plappa and Prologue connect by URL and accept plain http (`mockups/research.md`, *Surface: Audiobookshelf connection*), so a listener arriving from any of them expects the address they already use to work; "paste a URL and a token, press one button, read a plain result" is the one thing that surface must do, and (c) adds a state no board approved to a screen nobody drew. · **Read against:** the specification (FR-029, US6 #1, SC-010, A1, A8 `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`); the PRD (`docs/prd.md:82`, "connect by server URL and token"); the constitution's Principle VI (reached only through a driven port) and Principle IX ("Audiobookshelf server tokens, and any other credential a listener gives this system, MUST NOT be written to a log and MUST NOT be placed in a domain event" — an obligation over storage, not over the wire to the listener's own server); the mock-up research (*Surface: Audiobookshelf connection*, states and comparable products); the model (`LB1` example `https://books.home.lan`; `streams.connection`); the owner brief is unfilled, so no taste or tie-breaker of the owner's applies; no standing entry (D1–D37, ADRs 0001–0005 across every slice branch, text-searched) mentions the scheme. Cites: none — `.specify/domain/` holds only its README and states no fact about Audiobookshelf, TLS or self-hosting.
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-fable-5-1)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** a person extends Principle IX from what the service keeps to what it transmits — that a listener's token must not leave this service unencrypted on any path — which is a constitution amendment, not a run's decision; then (a), with the VPN and tunnel case decided alongside it, and `http://` connections already held lapse into "needs renewing".
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/examples.md` (*Not scenarios — held by the types*: the URL is an absolute http or https URL, the Q2 clause closed by D39; *Questions* Q2 → D39; R7 unchanged, since (b) adds no screen state)
- **Status:** standing

## D40 — Connecting to a different Audiobookshelf server than the one held: replace, or refuse?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB1 · **When:** 2026-10-21T16:25:09Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** Q3 in `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/examples.md`. A listener who holds a connection to one Audiobookshelf server (`https://books.home.lan`) sends `ConnectServer` for a different URL with a token that server accepts. The `connection` stream's rule says one connection at a time and that renewal replaces; it says nothing about a second server. Books already added from the first server are entries in the listener's library (LB4, LB15) addressed by their server item id, and US6 #5 says a connection change loses nothing of the library.
- **Options:** (a) **replace — the latest `ServerConnected` is the connection in force whichever server it names; books from the first server stay in the library as they are; a fetch or a push for one of them through the new connection fails as the server says it does and LB10 records it; no new event, no cross-stream guard; the screen says "Connected to <new host>" — recommended by the stage**; (b) refuse with a reason until the listener disconnects — needs a `ServerDisconnected` the model does not carry and FR-029 does not ask for, so a chart change on `main` that parks the slice; (c) replace, and warn on the screen before replacing that books from the old server will stop syncing.
- **Decision:** (a), as the stage recommended. `ConnectServer` for a different URL is handled exactly as a renewal: one more `ServerConnected` on `connection-{listenerId}` carrying the new `serverUrl`, the fold's connection in force is that latest event, and the credential port holds the new token and no longer the old (R5). Nothing on `book-{bookId}` is read or written; no refusal is added; the screen's connected state names the new host and nothing more. Written into R3 as its third bullet — *a different server → replaced, exactly as a renewal; books added from the first server stay in the library; whether their sync through the new connection succeeds is that server's answer, recorded by LB10* — and as scenario LB1-18. Not this slice's, and named so the slices that meet them ask rather than inherit a guess: `ServerBookAdded` carries the server item id and not the server it came from, so after a replacement LB5 and LB10 address that item on whichever server is in force — whether LB4's event should record its server is an event-field question for LB4's map (constitution XIV), and an item the new server does not hold is a third answer beside `unreachable | token rejected` for LB10's reason enumeration (Principle VI) when LB10 is mapped.
- **Why:** A self-hoster's server moves more often than it multiplies: the LAN name becomes a domain behind a reverse proxy, the box is rebuilt, the port changes. To Recap every one of those is "a different URL", and to the listener it is the same library at a new address, where every item id still holds — a refusal would stop exactly the listener who most needs to connect again, and the service cannot tell a moved server from a new one, so it does what it was asked. For the listener who really has two servers, (a) keeps everything the specification promises: their books stay in the library with their positions, caches and who's who (US6 #5; D11 says only removal deletes a book's things), and a sync that the new server will not answer is the same failure LB10 already records and LB12 already shows. (b) is not available to this run on the model it has — there is no disconnect to wait for, and inventing one is a chart change the map already ruled out — and even with one it would refuse the moved-server case for nothing. (c) would have this screen warn about books it cannot see: the connection stream knows no books, so the warning is a read over every `book-*` stream that LB4's screen owns and this one does not, and before any book has been added it would be false; it is also the warning D37 declined for the same reason — the library telling the listener about a rule it neither owns nor can see. The constitution decides the rest: the stream is the consistency boundary and a refusal conditioned on other streams is cross-stream work (Principle III), and simplicity governs — no requirement names the refusal. · **Read against:** the model (`streams.connection.because` in `docs/event-model/model.yaml`: "a listener has one Audiobookshelf connection at a time; renewing a rejected token replaces it rather than adding a second"; LB4's `ServerBookAdded` carrying "server item li_8x2"; LB5's `FetchOnAdd` "through the connection"; LB10's `ServerSyncFailed` "reason unreachable | token rejected"; LB15); the specification (FR-029, US6 #5 "nothing else about their library is lost", Key Entities *Audiobookshelf connection* "a server URL and token belonging to a listener", the *Audiobookshelf changes its API* edge case `specs/001-audiobook-recap/spec.md`); the constitution (Principle III, "The stream is the consistency boundary … Cross-stream work is a process manager"; *Additional Constraints*, "Simplicity governs: the smallest design satisfying the spec wins"; XIV, an event field is a stop-and-ask); standing D1 (the `connection-{listenerId}` row: "one connection at a time"), D11 (what removing a book deletes — and so what a connection change does not), D22 (on `slice/LB3`: the service does the deliberate thing the listener asked for and adds no refusal no requirement names), D37 (on `slice/LB8`: no warning from a context about a rule it does not own); the map's own R3, R5 and *Not this slice* (disconnecting by choice is left to the model). `.specify/product-owner.md` is still the template on every section, so no owner priority or taste bore on it. Cites: none — `.specify/domain/` holds only its README; decided from the model, the specification, the constitution and the standing entries above. (That Audiobookshelf library item ids are random and unique per server, which is what makes a pushed id on the wrong server a not-found rather than a collision, is a domain fact a person could file there; none is written, so none is cited, and the decision does not rest on it.)
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-fable-5-1)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** a beta self-hoster with books from two servers loses sync of the first's without having been told at the moment of connecting — then (c), the warning drawn by the screen that can see the connected books (LB4's, or LB12's), never (b), and the replacement itself stands.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/examples.md` (R3's third bullet; scenario LB1-18; Q3 closed). `docs/event-model/model.yaml` is untouched by this entry: the LB1 block's event keeps its fields and the connection stream's because-line already says this.
- **Status:** standing

## D41 — Where does a listener's Audiobookshelf token live, and how is it erased?
- **Stage:** plan · **Slice:** LB1 · **When:** 2026-10-21T16:38:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** Connecting keeps the listener's API token for LB5, LB9 and LB10 to reach the server with. The constitution forbids it in an event or a log (Principle IX) and asks that personal data be erasable without rewriting events; ADR 0004 (LB3) keeps personal data in the log by reference and names a value that is personal in itself as the case needing a mechanism of its own.
- **Options:** (a) **a driven port `ListenerCredentials` (`hold`, `forListener`, `release`) keyed by the listener's subject; a Postgres adapter with the token encrypted under AES-256-GCM by `CREDENTIALS_KEY` from the environment; the in-memory fake and the adapter under one contract suite; erasure is `release` — recommended by the stage**; (b) the token in `ServerConnected`, encrypted per listener (crypto-shredding in the log); (c) the token in clear in a table.
- **Decision:** (a). The event carries the listener's subject and the server URL and nothing else; the credential lives behind the port and every reader of the server asks the port. Held after the append, never before, so the credential follows the event that won a race (research P-2). Composition wires Postgres when `DATABASE_URL` and `CREDENTIALS_KEY` are both set and the in-memory adapter otherwise, saying so at start-up.
- **Why:** A listener hands Recap the key to their own server; what Recap keeps of it must be unreadable in a dump and gone when they ask. (b) makes every reader of the connection event a key lookup over ciphertext and turns the log into a credential store; (c) makes a database dump every listener's server. · **Read against:** the constitution (IX: tokens not in logs or events; secrets from the environment; erasure without rewriting events; IV: a driven port with a fake), ADR 0004 (on `slice/LB3`), the specification (FR-029, Key Entities *Audiobookshelf connection*), this project's own convention — a port with a fake and a contract suite over every adapter (`apps/recap-api/tests/contract/`, the event store's). Cites: none — `.specify/domain/` holds only its README.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the project gains a secret manager, which is then a second adapter behind the same port rather than a reversal.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/research.md` (P-2), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/data-model.md`, `docs/adr/0006-listener-credentials-held-behind-a-port.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D42 — How does the service prove a listener's token against their server, and what is the port every companion slice reaches the server through?
- **Stage:** plan · **Slice:** LB1 · **When:** 2026-10-21T16:38:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** R1 asks the server "the smallest question that proves the token"; R2 needs to tell a rejected token from a server that is not Audiobookshelf from one that cannot be reached. LB5, LB9 and LB10 will reach the same server through the same port, so its name and shape are theirs to copy.
- **Options:** (a) **one driven port `BookServer` — the listener's book server, named for the conversation and not the vendor — with `prove({ url, token }) → accepted | token-rejected | server-unreachable | not-audiobookshelf`, grown additively by the sibling that needs the next method; its Audiobookshelf adapter makes two calls pinned to v2.37.1: `GET /status` (unauthenticated; `app: "audiobookshelf"` or it is not one) then `GET /api/me` with the bearer (200 with `id` and `username` is accepted; 401 or 403 is rejected; network failure, timeout, 429 and 5xx are unreachable; a redirect is not followed) — recommended by the stage**; (b) one call, `GET /api/me`, reading a 401 as rejected and everything else as unreachable; (c) `POST /api/authorize`.
- **Decision:** (a). The `/status` probe is what makes `not-audiobookshelf` a classification rather than a guess; `/api/me` is the smallest authenticated question; a redirect not followed is what keeps the token on the origin the listener typed.
- **Why:** A listener who typed the wrong address should be told that, not that their token was rejected; and a listener's token should go to exactly one place. · **Read against:** the constitution (VI: a driven port this codebase owns, a stub pinned to a published contract, the failure modes enumerated and each tested; IV: no vendor name in a port); the Audiobookshelf source at its latest release (`server/Server.js`, `server/routers/ApiRouter.js`, `server/controllers/MeController.js` — research P-1 quotes the lines); the map's R1 and R2; D30 (LB6, the first write endpoint's conventions). Cites: none — `.specify/domain/` holds only its README.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** Audiobookshelf removes `/status` or stops stamping `app` on it, in which case the probe becomes `/ping` plus the shape of `/api/me`'s answer, behind the same port.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/research.md` (P-1), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/data-model.md`, `specs/001-audiobook-recap/contracts/LB1-connection.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D43 — A server progress at the position Recap already holds but with a later `lastUpdate`: adopted, or in step?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB9 · **When:** 2026-10-22T14:20:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** LB9 adopts the Audiobookshelf server's progress (`currentTime`, `lastUpdate`) as `PositionSyncedFromServer` when it is later-timed than what Recap holds; the model says only "refused when older than the position held". What happens when the server reports **the position Recap already holds with a later `lastUpdate`** — the ordinary case once LB10 pushes Recap's own position and the server stamps the push with its own clock, and the case of a second open with nothing changed? It decides whether every open appends an event, and which instant the gap LB6 names is measured from (D13, D27).
- **Options:** (a) **position identity first — a server position equal to the held one is *in step*: no event, the held instant stands; a different position is adopted when its `lastUpdate` is at or after `heldAt` (the position moves either way) and is `server-behind` when earlier — recommended by the stage**; (b) the instant rule alone: adopt whenever `lastUpdate` is later than `heldAt`, equal position or not, so the gap runs from LB10's push; (c) as (b) with a "position unchanged" flag on the event for every fold to special-case.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** "The position follows the Audiobookshelf app" — a position that has not moved has nothing to follow. The server's `lastUpdate` after a push is the server recording Recap's own report, not a listen, and under (b) a push delayed by a day would move the last-listened time to the push and tell the listener "it's been 1 day" about listening done nine days ago, which is the gap the offer (SC-003) and D4 rest on. (c) adds an event field for a reader-side special case in every fold (Principle XIV: a schema change is a stop-and-ask). The cost of (a) — a listener who rewinds on the server to exactly Recap's held second keeps Recap's older instant — is a position-exact coincidence. · **Read against:** the specification (US6 #2, #6; FR-011, FR-028; the *two devices* edge case), the model (`LB9` "refused when older than the position held"; `LB10` the outbound push; `streams.listening.because`, the later-timed report wins), standing D27 (the last-listened time is the latest instant held) and D33 (instants are compared, never clamped).
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the hand's walk or a beta listener shows a listen on the server that ended at Recap's exact held second being dated from Recap's older instant often enough to matter — then (c), at the cost of the event field.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB9/examples.md` (R2, R3) — first sent to the skipper by the run that wrote the map; that delegate ended on the harness's session limit before answering, so it was re-decided under decide: recommended-first
- **Status:** standing

## D44 — A book the listener marked finished on the server: what is adopted, and does `isFinished` enter the event?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB9 · **When:** 2026-10-22T14:20:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The server's progress record carries `isFinished` (and `progress`, `duration`) beside `currentTime` and `lastUpdate`; the model's `PositionSyncedFromServer` carries none of them and no reader of the stream reads them. Is a finished book a position like any other, and does `isFinished` enter the event? What Audiobookshelf does to `currentTime` when a book is marked finished or reset is a third party's behaviour, for the plan to cite from the published API — not decided here.
- **Options:** (a) **adopt `currentTime` as the server reports it, by the same rules as any other progress, and carry no finished flag — recommended by the stage**; (b) treat `isFinished: true` as the book's end, read from the book's chapters, whatever `currentTime` says; (c) carry `isFinished` on `PositionSyncedFromServer` for a later reader; (d) skip the sync when `isFinished` is true.
- **Decision:** (a). A finished book whose progress sits at its end is a position at the end (the *listener finishes the book* edge case: a recap of the whole book); one reset to zero is position 0, which the *position of zero* edge case already answers. The event keeps the shape the model drew.
- **Why:** The translation adopts what the server states and invents nothing (D33 never clamps a reported instant; D35 records only a value the listener named); (b) invents a position, (d) leaves Recap behind a server the listener used, and (c) is a field every reader carries for ever for a reader that does not yet exist (D38; Principle XIV). The smallest design satisfying the specification wins (*Additional Constraints*). · **Read against:** the specification (US6, FR-028, FR-029, the edge cases *The listener finishes the book* and *A position of zero*, A8), the constitution (Principles VI, XIV; *Additional Constraints*), standing D33, D35, D38.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the plan's research finds the published contract sets `currentTime` to something that is not the listener's position when a book is finished (a sentinel, or a value past the book's length) — then the plan raises it again rather than adopting it.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB9/examples.md` (R1, *Not scenarios*, *Questions*) — first sent to the skipper by the run that wrote the map; that delegate ended on the harness's session limit before answering, so it was re-decided under decide: recommended-first
- **Status:** standing

## D49 — Is a request made through the offer sheet recorded when the offer was already answered?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** CU4 · **When:** 2026-10-22T10:18:37Z · **Stream:** catch-up
- **Question:** An offer is answered at most once (FR-011, the stream's `because`), and `CU3` refuses a second *decline* of an answered offer. A request `via: offer` can arrive after the offer was declined on another device, or from a sheet left open past a decline. Is it recorded?
- **Options:** (a) **recorded like any other request, `via` kept as the client said it; the offer stays answered by whichever answer came first and nothing is refused on the offer's account — recommended by the example map**; (b) refused, *the offer is no longer open*, the way `CU3` refuses a second decline; (c) recorded with `via` rewritten to `button`.
- **Decision:** (a).

## D57 — Is a recap heard once per key, or once per playing?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** CU7 · **When:** 2026-10-22T11:22:56Z · **Stream:** catch-up

## D59 — Is the same thumb twice one thumb, and does a regeneration reset it?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** CU8 · **When:** 2026-10-22T13:00:49Z · **Stream:** catch-up

## D60 — What does `RecapOfferDeclined` carry?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** CU3 · **When:** 2026-10-22T13:12:00Z · **Stream:** catch-up
- **Question:** The model's event line reads *bookId, offer at 4:03:17, declinedAt* and its command line names two gestures, *declined | dismissed without choosing (D14)*. An event's fields are permanent (Principle VIII) and a field is a stop for an agent (Principle XIV). Two fields are implied and not named: the offer's instant, without which two offers at one position — a listener who declines, does not listen, and is offered again after another gap — cannot be told apart by any reader; and the gesture, without which D14's own reversal condition (*SC-003 shows most declines are dismissals*) can never be observed.

- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** `offeredAt` is what lets `CU2` and SC-003 match a decline to the offer it answers when a listener is offered twice at one position; `how` is the one field D14's *Would reverse if* needs, is a closed set of two, and is the kind of field Principle VIII warns about only when nothing reads it — the SC-003 analysis does, and the command already carries it. The listener who declined stays off the payload: who acted is the context's `actor_id`, the reading D26 took. · **Read against:** the model (`CU3`'s `cmd` and `evt` lines; `CU2`'s `RecapOffered` carries `offeredAt` and `position`), the specification (FR-011, SC-003, the dismissal edge case), D14 (its *Would reverse if*), D26, this project's convention (`CU4`'s `RecapRequested` copies what readers steer by and nothing personal; `CU1`'s `VoiceChosen` the same), the constitution (Principles VIII, IX, XIV)
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** `CU2` keys an offer by something other than its instant — then the event names the offer by that key and `offeredAt` stays as a plain fact

## D66 — Which addresses may the service reach when it proves a listener's Audiobookshelf token?
- **Stage:** review · **Slice:** LB1 · **When:** 2026-10-22T14:30:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The review of LB1 (finding 1, HIGH) found that `book-server-audiobookshelf.ts` fetches any http(s) address a signed-in listener types, including loopback, link-local (the cloud metadata address `169.254.169.254`) and the service's own internal hosts, and that the three distinct refusals let any external user map internal hosts and ports. `examples.md` R2 asked the plan to say "which addresses it may reach at all"; the plan left it to the trigger record.
- **Options:** (a) **refuse loopback (`127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`), link-local (`169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10` — the metadata ranges), unspecified (`0.0.0.0/8`, `::`), multicast and broadcast, and the IPv4-mapped forms of each; allow private ranges (RFC 1918, `fc00::/7`) and public addresses; the check is made on every address the name resolves to, at connect time on the address actually connected to (a `lookup` that filters, so a rebinding name cannot pass the check and connect elsewhere); a refused address answers `server-unreachable`, the same as a server that does not answer, so it is no oracle; loopback is permitted only when `BOOK_SERVER_ALLOW_LOOPBACK=true` (development and the demo's stub), never by default — recommended by the review**; (b) public addresses only — refuse private ranges too; (c) leave it open and record it for the capability's adversary pass.
- **Decision:** (a).
- **Why:** A self-hoster's Audiobookshelf is usually on a home network reached through a VPN or a tunnel, or beside Recap on the same private network, so refusing private ranges (b) refuses the beta's own first segment (SC-010, D39's reasoning). What no listener's server ever is, is the service's own loopback or the cloud's metadata endpoint, and those are exactly the addresses an attacker wants the service to call; refusing them closes the server-side request forgery the review found at the cost of nobody. Answering a refused address as unreachable keeps the listener's advice right ("check the address") and gives a scanner nothing it can tell apart. Checking at connect time rather than before the fetch is what makes the rule hold against a name that resolves differently the second time. (c) ships the hole behind a flag and hopes. · **Read against:** the constitution (IX, security and privacy; VI, the adapter enumerates its failure modes; IV, the predicate is a typed input with the default in the adapter); `examples.md` R2's bullet; D39 (http and https both accepted, the self-hoster's network is theirs); D42 (redirect not followed — the token stays on the origin typed); the method's default for SSRF (OWASP's SSRF prevention guidance: deny loopback, link-local and metadata, resolve and check the address connected to).
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** Recap is ever deployed somewhere its private network holds services a listener must not reach — then private ranges join the deny-list by configuration, and a self-hoster on a LAN connects through a public name.
- **Written to:** `apps/recap-api/src/adapters/driven/book-server-audiobookshelf.ts` and its test, `apps/recap-api/src/config.ts` (the optional BOOK_SERVER_ALLOW_LOOPBACK variable), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/research.md` (P-1), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/examples.md` (R2's addresses bullet closed), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB1/review.md`
- **Status:** standing

- **Decision:** (a). The read is a fold of one stream, as CU1's `GET /api/books/{bookId}/voice` is: it needs no projection and cannot disagree with the write. It answers `changedAt: null` when nothing was ever saved.
- **Why:** The method's rule against a command reading a view does not apply to the form reading its own stream; what it forbids is `ReadModel → Command`, and this is neither. Three more lines of route against a whole projection to keep in step with a stream that is never queried any other way. · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle II and III; the write model's own stream may be read); the model (`LB2` `folds`, no `reads`); CU1's contract (`GET /api/books/{bookId}/voice`) and D24; `docs/event-model/README.md` *`reads` and `folds` are different questions*; `Cites: none`.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** a second reader of the current settings appears that is not a fold of this stream, when a projection earns its place.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB2/examples.md` (R3), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/contracts/lb2-settings.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D75 — What is the idempotency key of a settings save, and is a save of unchanged values recorded?
- **Stage:** example map · **Slice:** LB2 · **When:** 2026-10-22T17:15:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** Principle II asks every public write for a caller-supplied key. LB1, LB3, LB6 and LB7 each carry one on the event (`connectionId`, `bookId`, `resumptionId`, `stopId`); the model's `SettingsChanged` has none, and `crud: true` says the stream is last-write-wins.
- **Options:** (a) **the save is a full replace: `PUT /api/settings` with all five values; a save equal to the values in force records nothing and answers the same body (idempotent by state, as CU1's repeat is), and an optional `Idempotency-Key` header that is a UUID becomes the event's correlation id — recommended**; (b) add a `changeId` to the event and the body, matching the siblings, at the cost of a field in a permanent contract (XIV) that nothing reads; (c) always append.
- **Decision:** (a). The event is exactly the model's: `listenerId`, `defaultTier`, `gapThreshold`, `voice`, `wifiOnly`, `prepareAhead`, `changedAt`. A retried save is the same body, so it finds the values already in force and appends nothing; a replay after a later save would overwrite it, which last-write-wins on a form accepts and the example map says so.
- **Why:** The key's purpose is that a repeat does not do the work twice, and for a full replace the stream state already says so. Adding a field to the event only to carry what the state proves is a permanent contract change for nothing, and (c) puts a row in the log for every tap on a form that autosaves. · **Read against:** the constitution (II, XIV); CU1's contract (R3, R-4, R-6: same-voice repeat answers 200 and records nothing; `Idempotency-Key` as correlation id); the model (`LB2`'s `crud: true` `because`); D1's `settings-{listenerId}` row ("last write wins on a form the listener edits"); `Cites: none`.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** a reader needs to tell two identical saves apart, when `changeId` is added as a new schema version.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB2/examples.md` (R2, R4), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/contracts/lb2-settings.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D83 — How does removal erase records that other slices own?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB15 · **When:** 2026-10-22T18:40:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** Position, last-listened time, recap cache, questions, answers, ratings and reports are written by slices that come before LB15 in the split (LB6–LB8, CU*) and do not exist on this tree. Does LB15 only emit `BookRemoved` for each owner's projection to fold, or does it name the erasure hook now (per-listener key shredding, D11, Principle IX)?
- **Options:** (a) emit `BookRemoved` only, each owner deletes its own records on folding it; (b) **name the erasure mechanism now and make `BookRemoved` its trigger: personal data in the log is encrypted under a per-subject key, removal shreds that key and deletes the projections and caches that fold the event**; (c) rewrite or delete events from the log.
- **Decision:** (b), split by ownership. LB15 owns the mechanism's contract — an ADR recording a key scope of listener plus book and `BookRemoved` as the only trigger. Each slice that persists personal data registers its records against that contract; projections and caches are deleted by folding `BookRemoved`. CS-6 is written against what exists on this tree: the erasure port is invoked with the listener and book and the hash-keyed transcription is untouched. Each later slice adds its own erasure example.
- **Why:** Principle IX says the mechanism MUST be designed before the first event carrying personal data is persisted, and (a) alone leaves events unerasable. Rewriting events (c) is ruled out by Principle IX. Key scope is per listener and book so removing one book leaves the others readable; account closure shreds every key a listener holds. · **Read against:** the constitution (Principle IX), the specification (FR-023, FR-043), D11; no `.specify/domain/` entry
- **Decided by:** sail-decide-skipper (claude-sonnet-5-5)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the plan finds reference-not-embed (personal data held outside the log) cheaper than shredding; that swaps the mechanism but keeps `BookRemoved` as the trigger.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB15/examples.md` (R4, CS-6), `docs/adr/0012-removal-erases-by-forgetting-keys.md` (written at the plan, Proposed)
- **Status:** awaiting human confirmation

## D91 — In what order are the event and the erasure written, and what finishes a half-done erasure?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** LB15 · **When:** 2026-10-22T19:05:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** `BookRemoved` is appended to the log and the keys are deleted from another store; no transaction spans them. What if the process stops between the two?
- **Options:** (a) **append `BookRemoved` first, then forget the keys; a repeated `RemoveBook` by the owner of a removed book runs the forgetting again before it answers "already removed"**; (b) forget first, then append; (c) an outbox and a background worker.
- **Decision:** (a). Forgetting nothing is not an error (the port says so), so the repeat is safe. A repeat whose forgetting throws is surfaced (503), never answered as done.
- **Why:** With (b) a crash after forgetting leaves a book the listener still sees but whose words are gone; with (a) the worst state is a book already gone from the library whose keys remain, and the listener can finish the erasure by removing it again. (c) adds a worker for a table delete that is idempotent. · **Read against:** ADR 0011 (`forget` is one `DELETE`), D83, Principle IX
- **Decided by:** host (standing decision D83)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the erasure grows beyond one idempotent call (several stores), when an outbox is cheaper than retrying by hand.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB15/examples.md` (CS-13), `docs/adr/0012-removal-erases-by-forgetting-keys.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D93 — What starts the fetch, and where does the automation's todo list live?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB5 · **When:** 2026-10-22T19:45:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The model's `FetchOnAdd` is an automation over `ServerBooksAwaitingAudio`. Nothing in the service runs in the background yet, and LB4's route must not hold a request open for a download of hundreds of megabytes. Principle III makes an automation's todo list persisted, VII asks every background job for a heartbeat, and `make check-model` refuses a `live` (folded per query) read model on an automation.
- **Options:** (a) `AddServerBook` fetches after its append; (b) a sweep that folds the log per query — refused by the model gate; (c) **an `async` read model: the projection `server-books-awaiting-audio`, one row per `ServerBookAdded` without an `AudioFetched`, maintained by the existing catch-up runner under a checkpoint (a new timestamped migration, a memory and a Postgres adapter behind one port), and a worker that sweeps the rows on an interval, one book at a time, writing a heartbeat line per sweep — recommended by the stage**; (d) a hand-made queue table written by LB4.
- **Decision:** (c), `materialisation: async`. The row is a hint and never a guard: before it acts on a row the use case reads the book's stream, which decides (Principle II). The projection is disposable — `reset` and a rebuild from position zero give the same rows.
- **Why:** (a) couples a slice in flight (LB4) to this one and holds a request on a download; (b) is what the gate and Principle III rule out; (d) makes LB4 write for LB5. (c) reuses the runner, checkpoint store and lease the scaffold ships, and the work a dead process abandoned is still owed in the table. · **Read against:** Principles II, III, VII; `projections.ts`; the model (`LB5`).
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the owner prefers the slice that appends `ServerBookAdded` (LB4) to write the row in its own transaction (`inline`).
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB5/examples.md` (R4, R5), `docs/event-model/model.yaml`
- **Status:** standing

## D94 — What does `AudioFetched` carry?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB5 · **When:** 2026-10-22T19:46:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The model says "bookId, audioHash sha256:…, 24 chapters from the file metadata, fetchedAt". Whether the chapters are a count or the list, and whether the listener is repeated, is not said.
- **Options:** (a) a count; (b) **the list, in `BookImported`'s chapter shape (`number`, optional `title`, whole `start`, `length` of at least 1), read from the fetched files — so preparation steers by the file's own chapters and not the server's listing; no `listenerId` (the stream's opening event names the owner); no URL, token, path, size or audio — recommended by the stage**.
- **Decision:** (b). Payload: `bookId`, `audioHash`, `chapters`, `fetchedAt`. The context carries `actor_id` `systems/fetch-on-add` acting on behalf of the listener, a fresh `correlation_id` per fetch and `causation_id: null` (stored events carry no identifier to point at).
- **Why:** A field is permanent (Principle VIII); preparation needs the located chapters of the bytes it will read, which can differ from the server's JSON, and a count would be a second fetch of the files to recover them. Ownership is already read from the book stream (ADR 0005). · **Read against:** ADR 0003, 0004, 0005; D86; the contract `LB4-server-book.md`.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** preparation turns out to want the book's duration too — an additive field.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB5/examples.md` (R1, R6), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/contracts/LB5-audio-fetch.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D95 — How is the audio obtained, and is its hash the one an upload would give?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB5 · **When:** 2026-10-22T19:47:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** FR-023 shares a transcription across listeners by the content hash of the audio. A fetched book's hash must mean the same thing as an imported one's, or sharing silently stops at the server boundary.
- **Options:** (a) **read the item's audio files one by one from the listener's server, stream each into the audio store's staging as an upload would be, describe them with the same metadata reader, and keep them — the store hashes the concatenation in the order LB3 derives from the files (ADR 0002) — recommended by the stage**; (b) download the item as one archive and unpack it; (c) hash on the server's reported checksum.
- **Decision:** (a). The same bytes yield the same `sha256:` as an import of them. Nothing is kept until every file has arrived and been read; a failed fetch leaves staging only, which the next attempt replaces and a success discards.
- **Why:** (b) needs an archive reader no manifest may gain on a slice branch; (c) trusts a vendor field we do not own (Principle VI). (a) reuses `AudioStore` and `AudioMetadata` exactly. · **Read against:** ADR 0002, FR-023, A10, Principle VI.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** Audiobookshelf items turn out to hold audio the file routes cannot serve one by one.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB5/examples.md` (R1, R2), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB5/research.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D96 — What happens when the audio cannot be fetched?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** LB5 · **When:** 2026-10-22T19:48:00Z · **Stream:** library
- **Question:** The model says the fetch is "skipped while the connection has lapsed". It names no event for a failure, and the server can fail in other ways (token rejected, unreachable, item gone, audio unreadable).
- **Options:** (a) append a failure event; (b) **record nothing: the book stays on the todo list and the next sweep tries again, so a reconnection resumes it without a command; each sweep's heartbeat line carries the counts and one reason per skipped book, and no book, token, address or listener — recommended by the stage**; (c) give up after N tries.
- **Decision:** (b). Every refusal is a skip: no connection, no credential or one held for another server (as D40/D42 read it), token rejected, unreachable, not Audiobookshelf, item not on the server, audio unreadable. A skipped book is not asked again at once: the process remembers when each was skipped and defers it for a minute, doubling after each further skip up to an hour — except a book skipped for want of a connection, which costs no request and is simply tried again at the next sweep, and does not use up the sweep's ceiling — and the sweep reads on down the list for books that are due — so a book the server will never give (a deleted item, a listener who never reconnects) cannot hold the ones behind it back. The memory is a hint: a restart forgets it, and the next sweep asks again.
- **Why:** An event nobody models and no screen reads would be permanent for a transient fact; a listener who reconnects expects the book to arrive. A stuck book costs a failed request a minute at first and one an hour in the end; surfacing "waiting for the server" is the library screen's (LB12) and reads the same list. · **Read against:** D40, D42, A8, Principle VII.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the owner wants the listener told why a book has no audio — then a modelled event.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/LB5/examples.md` (R3)
- **Status:** standing

## D97 — What starts preparation, and where does the automation's todo list live?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** PR1 · **When:** 2026-10-22T20:05:00Z · **Stream:** preparation
- **Question:** The model's `StartOnReceipt` is an automation over `AudioAwaitingPreparation`. Nothing in the service runs in the background that PR1 can lean on, and `BookImported` is appended inside a request that must not wait for a transcription. Principle III makes the todo list persisted; VII asks every background job for a heartbeat.
- **Options:** (a) the import and fetch use cases start preparation after their own append; (b) **a sweep — the todo list is the log itself: every audio hash named by a `BookImported` or `AudioFetched` with no `PreparationStarted` on `preparation-{audioHash}`, read types-only from the event store and folded per query; a worker started by the composition root runs it on an interval, one hash at a time, oldest first, and writes a heartbeat line per sweep — the shape LB5 took (D93), recommended by the stage**; (c) a persisted queue table.
- **Decision:** (b). The list is a fold of the write model, so it survives a restart and is guarded by the preparation stream's own version (an append at `NO_STREAM`), never by a read model. The sweep is the use case `startPendingPreparations`; the worker around it is tested with a fake timer; `main.ts` only starts it. Where LB5's worker has landed by then, the plan reuses its interval and heartbeat rather than a second one.
- **Why:** (a) couples two merged slices (LB3, LB5) to this one and makes the second import's answer wait on a fact about another listener's book; (c) adds a migration and a second source of truth for a fact the log holds. The one-stream guard is what US2 #6 asks for: whoever appends second finds the hash started and does nothing. The ceiling — a types-only read of every import — is D93's ceiling and fine at beta scale. · **Read against:** Principles II, III, VII; D93; FR-023, US2 #6; the model (`PR1`).
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the log grows until the per-sweep read is too slow — then a catch-up subscription with a checkpoint.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/PR1/examples.md` (R1, R2, R4, R5)
- **Status:** standing

## D98 — What does `PreparationStarted` carry, and whose chapters?
- **Stage:** example-map · **Slice:** PR1 · **When:** 2026-10-22T20:06:00Z · **Stream:** preparation
- **Question:** The model says "audioHash sha256:…, 31 chapters in order, startedAt". It does not say whether the chapters are a count or the list, whether the book or listener is named, or which book's chapters are used when several share a hash.
- **Options:** (a) a count; (b) **the list in `BookImported`'s chapter shape, no `bookId`, no `listenerId`, no title, taken from the first book recorded for the hash (log order) — recommended by the stage**; (c) the list plus the first book's id.
- **Decision:** (b). Payload: `audioHash`, `chapters`, `startedAt`; the context's actor is `systems/start-on-receipt` with no `on_behalf_of`. Identical bytes give identical chapters (LB3 and LB5 read them from the files), so which book is first changes nothing; if two disagree the first wins and the later hash is simply not on the list.
- **Why:** The stream is shared by every listener of the hash and FR-023 allows sharing the transcription, not who holds it; a book id or listener on it would be personal data on a stream nobody can erase per listener (LB15 erases by key, ADR 0012). A count would force PR2 to re-read the files to learn the chapters it must transcribe in order. A field is permanent (Principle VIII). · **Read against:** FR-020, FR-023, FR-043; Principles VIII, IX; D11; ADR 0004, 0012; `contracts/LB3-import-book.md`, `contracts/LB5-audio-fetch.md`.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** PR2 wants the duration too — an additive field.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/PR1/examples.md` (R1, R3), `specs/001-audiobook-recap/contracts/PR1-start-preparation.md`
- **Status:** standing

## D99 — Is a book that was removed before the sweep still prepared?
- **Stage:** gaps · **Slice:** PR1 · **When:** 2026-10-22T20:12:00Z · **Stream:** preparation
- **Question:** PR1's model reads `BookImported` and `AudioFetched`, not `BookRemoved`. A listener can import and remove a book between two sweeps; the hash may then be held by nobody.
- **Options:** (a) **prepare it anyway: the list is every hash any book of the stream log ever named, and removal never reaches preparation — recommended by the stage**; (b) read `BookRemoved` and skip a hash whose every book was removed — a model change (`reads`) and a second boundary per hash; (c) the sweep skips a book it cannot find an owner for.
- **Decision:** (a). The transcription is keyed by hash and outlives any one listener's copy (FR-043, D11, LB15 R4), so a removed book's hash is no different from one whose listener removed it a minute after it was prepared; the cost of one unwanted preparation is bounded by PR2's lazy policy (FR-027).
- **Why:** (b) puts a cross-stream read into the first automation of the fairway and changes the model's `reads` for a rare window; no requirement asks for it, and the simplicity rule says the smallest design that satisfies the specification wins. If the owner wants wasted transcription avoided, PR2's lazy policy is the place, because it already steers by positions. · **Read against:** FR-027, FR-043; D11; Principle on simplicity; LB15 R4; the model (`PR1` reads).
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** medium · **Would reverse if:** the cost of transcribing removed books shows up in SC-007's cost per book — then the model adds `BookRemoved` to PR1's `reads`.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/PR1/examples.md` (R4, PR1-17)
- **Status:** standing

## D100 — Where does PR1's todo list live, given the model refuses a per-query fold for an automation?
- **Stage:** plan · **Slice:** PR1 · **When:** 2026-10-22T21:10:00Z · **Stream:** preparation
- **Question:** D97 put the todo list in the log itself, folded per query (`materialisation: live`). `make check-model` refuses `live` for an automation ("a todo list is persisted — `inline` or `async`"), the constitution (III) says an automation's todo list MUST be persisted, and `docs/event-model/README.md` says a slice declaring `async` and shipping an in-request fold is the same mistake. The slice cannot reach `planned` as D97 wrote it.
- **Options:** (a) keep D97 and declare `live` — refused by the gate; (b) `inline` — the append that names the hash is LB3's and LB5's, which this slice may not touch; (c) **`async`: a catch-up projection `audio-awaiting-preparation` over the log with a checkpoint (the project's `catchUp` runner and `CheckpointStore`), whose view holds one row per named hash — the todo list the sweep reads; the sweep catches the projection up, lists the hashes not started, oldest first, and still decides each start from the hash's own stream — recommended by the stage (the README and the gate)**.
- **Decision:** (c). D97's other halves stand: the sweep, the worker on an interval with a heartbeat, one hash at a time oldest first, the append at `NO_STREAM` as the guard. What changes is only where the list is read from: a view derived from `BookImported`, `AudioFetched` and `PreparationStarted` (hash, the chapters of the first naming event, its log position, and whether a start was seen — a row is kept, not deleted, so a later book with the same hash does not re-list it), written in the unit of work that moves the checkpoint, rebuildable from zero. The view is a hint: the write model decides (PR1-4, PR1-7, PR1-8, PR1-23 are unchanged). A Postgres adapter and its migration persist the view; the in-memory adapter serves the unit tests and a process with no database.
- **Why:** The gate and the constitution are a floor, not an option, and the README's own reason holds here too (a standalone run must find work it did not create) — the log fold would have met the reason but not the declaration. The cost is a table, a migration and one more adapter; the benefit is the ceiling D97 accepted (a types-only read of every import per sweep) goes away. · **Read against:** constitution III, `docs/event-model/README.md` (*A processor is a role, not a deployment*), the model checker's `materialisation` rule, `src/projections.ts`, `src/application/ports/read-models.ts`, D93, D97.
- **Decided by:** host (stage recommendation)
- **Confidence:** high · **Would reverse if:** the model's rule on automations changes — then D97's fold returns.
- **Written to:** `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/PR1/plan.md`, `specs/001-audiobook-recap/slices/PR1/examples.md` (R4), `docs/event-model/model.yaml`
- **Status:** standing
